# Plots

Your board prints `23.5`, then `23.6`, once a second. A **Plot** turns that stream into a line that scrolls across the screen, newest reading at the right edge.

```cpp
Serial.println(temp);   // sends 23.5 and a newline: one frame, one value, one moving line
```

If you have no project yet, follow [Getting Started](Getting-Started.md) first. Then, in the [Project Editor](Project-Editor.md), select the dataset that holds the value and tick its **Plot** widget (`graph: true` on the dataset in the project file).

## Plot and Multi-Plot

A **Plot** shows one dataset (enable it with `graph: true`). A **Multi-Plot** overlays several signals from one group on a shared axis with a color legend, which suits comparing channels such as the three axes of an accelerometer (set the group's widget to Multi-Plot). Both are configured in the Project Editor.
docs.title: Plots#0

docs.body:
| You want to                           | Use                                                            |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| Watch one signal over time            | Plot                                                           |
| Compare several signals on one chart  | Multi-Plot                                                     |
| Plot one value against another        | Plot with a custom X axis                                      |
| Hold a repeating waveform still       | Plot or Multi-Plot with Sweep (Pro)                            |
| See a frequency spectrum              | FFT Plot (see [Widget Reference](Widget-Reference.md#fft-plot)) |
docs.title: Plots#1

docs.body:
## How the X axis works

Time is the default. Change it with the **X-Axis Source** field in the Project Editor (`xAxis` in the project file): on a dataset it offers Time, Samples, or another dataset; on a Multi-Plot group it offers Time or Samples.

| X axis      | Set by X-Axis Source                              | Reads as                                  |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| **Time**    | Time (default)                                    | Seconds, newest sample at the right       |
| **Samples** | Samples                                           | Sample index, 0 to N, newest at the right |
| **Custom**  | Another dataset (Plot only)                       | That dataset's value (XY / scatter)       |
docs.title: Plots#2

docs.body:
A **time** plot scrolls: it shows the most recent window of data, as wide as the dashboard time range, with the newest reading pinned at the right edge. A **custom X axis** plots one dataset against another instead of against time, which gives XY traces such as a phase plot or an I-V curve.

Two settings control how much history a plot keeps:
docs.title: Plots#3

docs.body:
| Setting         | Meaning                                         | Range and default                                                            | Where                                                                                 |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Time Range**  | Width of the scrolling time window              | Presets: 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 ms; 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 30, 60, 120, 300 s. Typed values snap to the nearest. Default 10 s.  | Project Editor toolbar (saved as `plotTimeRange`) and Preferences, Plotting tab       |
| **Point Count** | Samples kept per signal (window width on a Samples plot) | 10 to 100000 in steps of 10. Default 1000.                           | Project Editor toolbar (saved as `pointCount`) and Preferences, Plotting tab          |
docs.title: Plots#4

docs.body:
The Project Editor values are saved into the project file; the Preferences dialog applies them to the live dashboard.

The Y axis auto-scales to the data by default. Pin it with `plotMin` / `plotMax` in the project file (the Y-axis minimum and maximum fields in the Project Editor), or from the **Axis Range** dialog on the toolbar. **Logarithmic Y Axis** scales it in decades, and values at or below zero are drawn at the bottom. **Logarithmic X Axis** (Project Editor, dataset form) is available when X-Axis Source is Samples or another dataset, not Time.

## Toolbar controls

When a plot is large enough to show its toolbar, these controls appear left to right:
docs.title: Plots#5

docs.body: | Control | Icon | What it does | |---------|------|--------------| | **Interpolation** | | Cycles line style: none (raw points), linear, ZOH (stepped: holds the last value until the next sample), or stem (a vertical line from zero to each point). | | **Area** | | Plot only. Fills the region under the curve. Enabled for linear and ZOH; disabled for none and stem. | | **X / Y label** | | Shows or hides each axis label. | | **Crosshair** | | Shows a tracking crosshair that follows the cursor. | | **Pause / Resume** | | Freezes this plot. Readings that arrive while paused are not drawn after Resume. Other widgets keep updating. | | **Sweep / Trigger Mode** | | Turns [Sweep / Trigger mode](#sweep--trigger-mode-pro) on or off. A repeating waveform holds still, like on an oscilloscope (Pro, time-axis plots only). | | **Trigger Settings** | | Opens the trigger settings (Pro). Enabled only while Sweep is on. | | **Past sweeps** | A stepper with `‹` and `›` arrows | Plot only. Shown next to Trigger Settings while Sweep is on. Keeps 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64 earlier sweeps drawn behind the live trace, dimmed by age. | | **Reset View** | | Returns pan and zoom to the default view. | | **Axis Range Settings** | | Opens the Axis Range dialog to set fixed minimum and maximum values for the axes. The button shows the gear (Preferences) icon. |
docs.title: Plots#6

docs.body:
Drag inside the plot to pan and scroll to zoom; **Reset View** undoes both. These buttons and the toolbars of every other widget are catalogued in the [Toolbar & Button Reference](Toolbar-Reference.md#plot).

## Sweep / Trigger mode (Pro)

A scrolling sine wave slides past too fast to read, like carriage numbers on a passing train. **Sweep / Trigger mode** works the way a benchtop oscilloscope does: every sweep starts at the same point on the waveform, so the trace holds still and you can read it.

Sweep / Trigger is Pro and works only on plots with a Time X axis; otherwise, or without a license, the Sweep and Trigger Settings buttons are hidden. The first Pro-feature use shows a Yes/No prompt offering a trial, which needs an internet connection to register. See [Pro vs Free](Pro-vs-Free.md).
docs.title: Plots#7

docs.body:
Turn it on with the **Sweep** button, then open **Trigger Settings**. For a first stable trace, set **Level** to the middle of your signal (0 for a sine that swings from -1 to 1), **Slope** to Rising, **Mode** to Auto, and **Timebase** to two or three cycles of the signal.

### Trigger: what starts each sweep

In Sweep / Trigger mode (Pro), the Trigger Settings dialog sets the **trigger**, the event that begins a new sweep. You choose the value the signal must cross (the **Level**) and the direction of the crossing (the **Slope**, Rising or Falling). Each time the signal crosses that level in that direction, a fresh sweep starts there, which keeps successive sweeps aligned. While the dialog is open, a horizontal line on the plot marks the Level; drag it to change Level and the dialog field follows.
docs.title: Plots#8

docs.body:
There are three **modes**:

| Mode       | Behavior                                                                  |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Auto**   | Triggers on a crossing, and free-runs anyway if none is found. Always moving. |
| **Normal** | Triggers only on a crossing. The trace holds the last sweep until the next one. |
| **Single** | Captures one sweep, then stops. Use **Capture Next** to arm another.      |

Auto is the everyday choice. Use Normal for an intermittent signal you don't want redrawn by noise, and Single to freeze one event.
docs.title: Plots#9

docs.body:
On a **Multi-Plot**, the **Source** setting picks which curve the trigger watches. All curves are captured together and stay aligned to that one signal.

### Timing: width and rate

In Sweep / Trigger mode (Pro), the **Timebase:** field in Trigger Settings sets how much time one sweep shows, in milliseconds. Leave it empty (the field reads "Match time range") to use the plot's full time range. Lower it to zoom in: a shorter timebase shows fewer cycles but draws them larger, which is the setting to reach for when a fast waveform looks like a solid band. The trace begins at the left edge, time zero, and runs for one timebase to the right.
docs.title: Plots#10

docs.body:
A Timebase longer than the plot's time range is capped at the time range.

The **Holdoff:** field, also in milliseconds (default 0), ignores new triggers for that long after each one. Raise it when a complex waveform crosses the level several times per cycle and you want to lock onto just the first crossing.

## Performance

A plot redraws at the **UI Refresh Rate** (Preferences, Plotting tab; 1 to 240 Hz).
docs.title: Plots#11

docs.body:
# Plugin Development

## Overview

Your device prints readings, and you want every frame in a database, or an FFT window Serial Studio does not draw. A plugin is that script: a small program (Python is the easiest) that Serial Studio launches and that talks to it over localhost.

Plugins can be written in any language (Python, C++, Go, Rust, Node.js) and are installed and started from the [Extension Manager](Extensions.md), which you open with the **Extensions** toolbar button. This page is for writing one; to install one, see [Extensions](Extensions.md).

Plugins and the default repository work in the free edition. Adding, listing or removing other repositories (Repository Settings and the `extensions.*Repository` commands) requires Serial Studio Pro, see [Pro vs Free](Pro-vs-Free.md).
docs.title: Plugin-Development#0

docs.body:
## How Plugins Work

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Serial Studio] -->|"commands and frames (JSON lines), port 7777"| B[Plugin process]
    A -->|"optional frame streaming (needs grpc: true), port 8888"| B
```

1. You install the plugin from the Extension Manager.
2. You open the plugin in the Extension Manager and click **Run**.
3. If the API Server is off, Serial Studio asks "API Server Required". **Yes** turns it on and launches the plugin; **No** cancels the launch.
4. The plugin connects to Serial Studio and starts sending commands or reading data.
5. You click **Stop** (or quit Serial Studio) to end the plugin.
docs.title: Plugin-Development#1

docs.body:
Serial Studio also stops running plugins when the device disconnects and relaunches them when a device connects again, except plugins you stopped yourself or that exited on their own. Plugins do not run in a deployment package session, see [Operator Deployments](Operator-Deployments.md).

The API Server is the local server Serial Studio exposes for scripts. It is off by default and listens on port 7777. The gRPC server (port 8888, a faster streaming protocol you only need at high frame rates) runs only while the API Server is on. If you start your script yourself, or test with `nc`, turn on **Preferences > General > API & Plugins > Enable API Server** first. The port is the **API Server Port** field below it.
docs.title: Plugin-Development#2

docs.body:
## Getting Started

### Minimal Python Plugin (TCP/JSON)

Create a folder with two files.

`info.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "my-first-plugin",
  "type": "plugin",
  "title": "My First Plugin",
  "description": "Prints connection status every second.",
  "author": "Your Name",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "entry": "plugin.py",
  "runtime": "python3",
  "terminal": true,
  "files": ["info.json", "plugin.py"]
}
```

`plugin.py`:

```python
import json
import socket
import time

sock = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 7777))
lines = sock.makefile("r")

def send_command(command, params=None):
    msg = {"type": "command", "id": "1", "command": command}
    if params:
        msg["params"] = params
    sock.sendall((json.dumps(msg) + "\n").encode())
    while True:
        msg = json.loads(lines.readline())
        if msg.get("type") == "response" and msg.get("id") == "1":
            return msg
docs.title: Plugin-Development#3

docs.body:
while True:
    result = send_command("io.getStatus")
    print(f"Connected: {result.get('result', {}).get('isConnected')}")
    time.sleep(1)
```

While a device is streaming, the server also pushes frame batches, raw data and lifecycle events on the same socket. Reading line by line and matching responses by `id`, as above, keeps them apart. See [Server-Push Messages](API-Reference.md#server-push-messages).

To try it in two minutes, turn on the API Server (**Preferences > General > API & Plugins > Enable API Server**), save `plugin.py` and run `python3 plugin.py`. It prints `Connected: False` once a second until a device connects, then `True`. It is not much, but it is a plugin.
docs.title: Plugin-Development#4

docs.body:
To run it from the Extension Manager instead, the folder needs a `manifest.json` and a SHA-256 digest for `plugin.py`, and installing a local folder needs Serial Studio Pro. The `info.json` above lists `plugin.py` without a digest, so add one first (see [File Digests](#file-digests) and [Testing Your Plugin](#testing-your-plugin)). Started from the Extension Manager, a terminal window opens and the plugin runs only while a device is connected, so it prints `Connected: True`.

### Minimal Python Plugin (gRPC)

For sustained frame streaming, use gRPC. The TCP/JSON example is enough to start, so skip this until you need high frame rates.
docs.title: Plugin-Development#5

docs.body:
You need `pip install grpcio grpcio-tools` and the two generated stub files; the `protoc` command is in the [gRPC Server](gRPC-Server.md) guide.

`info.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "my-grpc-plugin",
  "type": "plugin",
  "title": "My gRPC Plugin",
  "description": "Streams frames via gRPC.",
  "author": "Your Name",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "entry": "plugin.py",
  "runtime": "python3",
  "grpc": true,
  "files": [
    "info.json",
    "plugin.py",
    "serialstudio_pb2.py",
    "serialstudio_pb2_grpc.py"
  ]
}
```

`plugin.py`:

```python
import grpc
import serialstudio_pb2 as pb
import serialstudio_pb2_grpc as rpc
docs.title: Plugin-Development#6

docs.body:
channel = grpc.insecure_channel("localhost:8888")
stub = rpc.SerialStudioAPIStub(channel)

print("Streaming frames...")
for batch in stub.StreamFrames(pb.StreamRequest()):
    for frame in batch.frames:
        print(frame.frame)
```

Any API command also runs over gRPC with `stub.ExecuteCommand(pb.CommandRequest(id="1", command="io.getStatus"))`.

### Choosing a Transport

| Transport | Port | Use it for | How to enable |
|-----------|------|------------|---------------|
| TCP/JSON | 7777 | Commands, lifecycle events and your first plugin. | API Server on. See the [API Reference](API-Reference.md). |
| gRPC | 8888 | Sustained frame streaming. | API Server on and `"grpc": true` in `info.json`. See [gRPC Server](gRPC-Server.md). |
docs.title: Plugin-Development#7

docs.body:
## Plugin Structure

A plugin lives in its own folder inside a repository:

```
plugin/my-plugin/
  info.json          # Required: metadata and entry point
  plugin.py          # Entry point script
  requirements.txt   # Optional: Python dependencies
  run.sh             # Optional: launcher for macOS/Linux
  run.cmd            # Optional: launcher for Windows
  serialstudio_pb2.py       # Optional: gRPC stubs
  serialstudio_pb2_grpc.py  # Optional: gRPC stubs
```

### Launcher Scripts

A launcher script (`run.sh` or `run.cmd`) installs dependencies into a local venv, sets environment variables, or starts a native binary without a runtime. Set `"runtime": ""` in `info.json`. If you omit `runtime`, Serial Studio runs `run.sh` through `python3`.
docs.title: Plugin-Development#8

docs.body:
`run.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

if [ ! -d "venv" ]; then
    python3 -m venv venv
    ./venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
fi

./venv/bin/python plugin.py
```

`run.cmd` follows the same pattern with `python -m venv venv`, `venv\Scripts\pip` and `venv\Scripts\python`.

## info.json Reference
docs.title: Plugin-Development#9

docs.body:
| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | Yes | Unique identifier (lowercase, hyphens). Must be unique across all extensions. |
| `type` | Yes | Must be `"plugin"`. |
| `title` | Yes | Display name in the Extension Manager. |
| `description` | Yes | Short description shown on the card. |
| `author` | Yes | Author name or organization. |
| `version` | Yes | Semantic version string (e.g., `"1.0.0"`). |
| `license` | No | License identifier (e.g., `"MIT"`, `"GPL-3.0"`). |
| `category` | No | Category for filtering in the Extension Manager. |
| `screenshot` | No | Relative path to a preview image. |
| `files` | Yes | Array of relative file paths to install. Must include `info.json` itself. Every file except `info.json` also needs a SHA-256 digest, see [Packaging and Distribution](#packaging-and-distribution). |
| `entry` | Yes | Script or binary entry point (e.g., `"plugin.py"`, `"run.sh"`). |
| `runtime` | No | The program that runs `entry` (e.g., `"python3"`). Default: `python3`. Use `""` for native binaries and launcher scripts. |
| `terminal` | No | `true` to launch in a system terminal window, which shows the plugin's output and errors while you debug; the output then goes to that window instead of the plugin log. Default: `false`. On macOS the entry file is opened in Terminal and `runtime` is not applied, so give a launcher script with a shebang. On Linux Serial Studio tries `x-terminal-emulator`, `gnome-terminal`, `konsole`, `xfce4-terminal`, then `xterm`, and runs without a terminal if none is installed. |
| `grpc` | No | `true` if the plugin uses gRPC (port 8888). A build without gRPC support refuses to launch the plugin. Default: `false`. |
| `platforms` | No | Per-platform overrides (see [Platform-Specific Builds](#platform-specific-builds)). |
| `dependencies` | No | Array of `{name, executables, url, pip}`. Serial Studio checks `executables` on `PATH` before launch. |
| `icon` | No | Relative path to an image, shown next to the plugin in the Extension Manager's installed-plugins list. |
docs.title: Plugin-Development#10

docs.body:
Before launch, Serial Studio looks for each `executables` entry on `PATH` and shows a "Missing Dependency" dialog with a link to `url` if none is found (**Yes** opens the page, and the launch is cancelled either way). An entry with a `pip` key skips that check; Serial Studio does not run `pip` itself, it only logs "[Setup] Installing required packages" when no `venv` folder exists, so install the packages from your launcher script:

```json
"dependencies": [
  { "name": "Python", "executables": ["python3", "python"], "url": "https://www.python.org/downloads/" }
]
```

### Full Example
docs.title: Plugin-Development#11

docs.body:
```json
{
  "id": "signal-analyzer",
  "type": "plugin",
  "title": "Signal Analyzer",
  "description": "Real-time FFT and spectral analysis of incoming data.",
  "author": "Example Corp",
  "version": "2.1.0",
  "license": "MIT",
  "category": "Analysis",
  "screenshot": "screenshot.png",
  "entry": "plugin.py",
  "runtime": "python3",
  "grpc": true,
  "files": [
    "info.json",
    "plugin.py",
    "analyzer.py",
    "serialstudio_pb2.py",
    "serialstudio_pb2_grpc.py",
    "requirements.txt",
    "screenshot.png"
  ],
  "platforms": {
    "darwin/*":    { "entry": "run.sh",  "runtime": "", "files": ["run.sh"] },
    "linux/*":     { "entry": "run.sh",  "runtime": "", "files": ["run.sh"] },
    "windows/*":   { "entry": "run.cmd", "runtime": "", "files": ["run.cmd"] }
  }
}
```
docs.title: Plugin-Development#12

docs.body:
## Platform-Specific Builds

Plugins can provide different entry points for each operating system and architecture with the `platforms` field in `info.json`:

```json
"platforms": {
  "darwin/*":        { "entry": "run.sh",  "runtime": "", "files": ["run.sh"] },
  "linux/x86_64":   { "entry": "run.sh",  "runtime": "", "files": ["run.sh", "bin/analyzer-linux-x64"] },
  "linux/arm64":    { "entry": "run.sh",  "runtime": "", "files": ["run.sh", "bin/analyzer-linux-arm64"] },
  "windows/*":      { "entry": "run.cmd", "runtime": "", "files": ["run.cmd", "bin/analyzer.exe"] }
}
```

Platform keys use the format `os/arch` or `os/*` (for universal builds). `darwin` is macOS.
docs.title: Plugin-Development#13

docs.body:
| Key | Matches |
|-----|---------|
| `darwin/*` | macOS (any architecture) |
| `darwin/arm64` | macOS Apple Silicon only |
| `linux/x86_64` | Linux x86_64 |
| `linux/arm64` | Linux ARM64 (Raspberry Pi, etc.) |
| `windows/*` | Windows (any architecture) |
| `windows/x86_64` | Windows x86_64 only |
| `*` | Any platform (generic fallback) |

Resolution order: exact `os/arch` key first, then `os/*`, then `*`.

- Platform-specific `files` are **merged** with the base `files` array during installation.
- If a plugin has no matching platform entry, the **Install** button is disabled and an **Unavailable** badge is shown.
- If no `platforms` field is present, the plugin is assumed to work on all platforms.
docs.title: Plugin-Development#14

docs.body:
## State Persistence

Plugin state (window positions, settings, configurations) is saved in the project file alongside widget layout data. Different projects can have different plugin configurations.

Serial Studio never calls `extensions.saveState` on its own. Call it from your plugin after any change worth restoring, not only on the `disconnected` event: Serial Studio stops running plugins when the device disconnects, so a save on that event can race the shutdown. Call `extensions.loadState` when the plugin starts and when a device connects, since the project may have changed. Both commands are Confirm-tier in the API safety table, so an AI-driven plugin can meet a confirmation prompt.
docs.title: Plugin-Development#15

docs.body:
`send_command` is the helper from [Getting Started](#minimal-python-plugin-tcpjson):

```python
send_command("extensions.saveState", {
    "pluginId": "my-plugin",
    "state": {"windowX": 100, "windowY": 200, "zoom": 1.5}
})

result = send_command("extensions.loadState", {"pluginId": "my-plugin"})
state = result.get("result", {}).get("state", {})
```

### Auto-Relaunch

Plugins that were running when the device disconnected are relaunched at the next connection, except the ones you stopped yourself. A plugin that exits on its own while a device is connected is not relaunched either.

## Lifecycle Events
docs.title: Plugin-Development#16

docs.body:
The API Server broadcasts events to all connected TCP/JSON clients as standalone JSON lines. gRPC clients do not receive them; they can poll `io.getStatus` or watch stream activity instead.

| Event | When | Typical Plugin Action |
|-------|------|----------------------|
| `{"event": "connected"}` | The I/O connection comes up | Start processing, restore state |
| `{"event": "disconnected"}` | The I/O connection goes down | Pause processing |

On disconnect Serial Studio also terminates the plugin, so treat `disconnected` as a short warning, not a pause hook. Read the events from the socket's line reader (`lines = sock.makefile("r")`, as in [Minimal Python Plugin](#minimal-python-plugin-tcpjson)):
docs.title: Plugin-Development#17

## Testing Your Plugin

### Manual Testing

In the free edition, turn on the API Server and run `python3 plugin.py` yourself while you develop. The steps below install the plugin through the Extension Manager and need Serial Studio Pro.

1. Create a folder with your `info.json` and plugin files, and a `manifest.json` beside it (see [Packaging and Distribution](#packaging-and-distribution)).
2. Add the folder as a repository with **Browse** in Repository Settings, then click **Install** on the plugin.
3. Click **Run** in the Extension Manager detail view.
4. Read the plugin's output and errors in the log on the Extension Manager detail view, or set `"terminal": true` to read them in the terminal window that opens.
docs.title: Plugin-Development#20

docs.body:
Copying files into the Extensions folder by hand does not work: Run refuses a plugin Serial Studio has not installed.

### Testing the API Connection

Before building a full plugin, test the connection on its own. `nc` (netcat) is included with macOS and Linux; on Windows, run the [minimal Python plugin](#minimal-python-plugin-tcpjson) with `python plugin.py` instead.

```bash
# TCP/JSON
echo '{"type":"command","id":"1","command":"io.getStatus"}' | nc localhost 7777

# gRPC (grpcurl is a command-line gRPC client)
grpcurl -plaintext localhost:8888 serialstudio.SerialStudioAPI/ListCommands
```
docs.title: Plugin-Development#21

docs.body:
### Common Issues

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Connection refused | Script started outside Serial Studio and API Server off | Turn on Preferences > General > API & Plugins > Enable API Server. The port is the API Server Port field below it (default 7777). |
| `grpcio` import error | Package not installed | `pip install grpcio grpcio-tools` |
| Plugin exits immediately | Unhandled exception, which stays invisible until you look at the output | Read the log on the Extension Manager detail view, or set `"terminal": true` to watch it in a terminal window. |
| No frames streaming | Device not connected, API Server off, or a gRPC plugin without `"grpc": true` | Connect a device. For a gRPC plugin, confirm the API Server is on and `"grpc": true` is in `info.json`. |

docs.body:
## Packaging and Distribution

### Repository Structure

```
my-extensions-repo/
  manifest.json
  plugin/my-plugin/
    info.json
    plugin.py
    run.sh
    run.cmd
    requirements.txt
    screenshot.png
```

### manifest.json

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "repository": "My Extensions",
  "extensions": [
    "plugin/my-plugin/info.json"
  ]
}
```

### File Digests

Serial Studio refuses to install a file it cannot verify, local folders included. Every file in `files` except `info.json` needs a 64-character hex SHA-256 digest (uppercase is normalised to lowercase). Give it inline:

```json
"files": [
  "info.json",
  { "path": "plugin.py", "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex characters>", "size": 1234 }
]
```
docs.title: Plugin-Development#23

docs.body:
or keep `files` a plain list and add a `sha256` table beside it:

```json
"sha256": { "plugin.py": { "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex characters>", "size": 1234 } }
```

If any file other than `info.json` has a missing or malformed digest, Serial Studio refuses the whole extension, and the Problem Center shows an "Extension ... cannot be verified" warning.

### Hosting Options

Repository Settings and `extensions.addRepository` require Serial Studio Pro on the installing user's side.

- **GitHub**: Push to a repository and share the raw manifest URL, for example `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/your-org/extensions/main/manifest.json`.
- **Local folder**: Use **Browse** in Repository Settings to point to a local folder during development.
- **Any web server over https://**: Relative paths in `files` resolve against the `info.json` URL. Plain `http://` is refused with "Repositories must be a local folder or an https:// URL."
docs.title: Plugin-Development#24

docs.body:
### Installation Path

Installed plugins live in `Extensions/plugin/your-plugin/` inside your Serial Studio workspace folder, which defaults to `Documents/Serial Studio` (Windows: `Documents\Serial Studio`).

# Preferences

The plot scrolls past too fast, the text is too small, or you want a dark theme. Preferences is where all of that lives. It is available in every edition; the **Notifications** tab and **Save Videos by Default** are Pro only.

Click **Preferences** on the main toolbar, click **Settings** on the dashboard taskbar (the same dialog), or search for Preferences in the [command palette](Command-Palette.md). On macOS the shortcut is **Cmd+,**.

To make a plot show the last 30 seconds, open the **Plotting** tab and choose 30 s from the **Time Range** list. For bigger text, open **Layout** and change **Font Size**; for a dark theme, pick one under **Theme** on the **General** tab.
docs.title: Preferences#0

docs.body:
Changes apply as you make them, so **Apply** and **Close** both just close the dialog. These settings need a restart:

- **Rendering Backend**, **Display Scaling**, **Custom Scale (%)**, and **HDR Output**, all on the **Startup** tab. Serial Studio prompts for the restart when you change one.
- **Custom Window Decorations** (**General** tab), **Apply Performance Hints**, and **Keep Display Awake** (**Startup** tab). They take effect the next time Serial Studio starts, with no prompt.

## Reset

**Reset**, at the bottom left of the dialog, restores defaults on every tab at once, except the settings listed below. It turns **Enable API Server** and **Allow External API Connections** off, sets **Theme** to Default and **Custom Scale (%)** to 100, and returns **Rendering Backend** to Automatic and **Display Scaling** to Fractional where the platform lets you change them. It leaves these as they are:
docs.title: Preferences#1

docs.body:
- **Language**, **Icon Pack**, **Widget Toolbar Icons**, and **Workspace Folder**
- **HDR Output**, **SIMD Instruction Set**, and **API Server Port**
- **Row Interval (ms)** and the two extension update switches

## General
docs.title: Preferences#2

## Startup

If a launch with a non-automatic **Rendering Backend** crashes, the next launch returns to **Automatic (Platform Default)**. If a launch with **HDR Output** on crashes, the next launch turns it off.

### HDR Output

Skip this unless you have an HDR display. On one, **HDR Output** lets the parts of the dashboard that carry a live signal glow brighter than the white of the interface, so a needle or a lit lamp stands out while everything else looks the same.

HDR Output is free in every edition. The row exists on macOS with Metal and on Windows with Direct3D 11, which is what **Automatic (Platform Default)** selects there. Linux has no HDR path, and the row disappears on Windows when **Rendering Backend** is OpenGL, Vulkan, or **Software (Fallback)**.
docs.title: Preferences#6

docs.body:
| Element | Brightness, relative to interface white |
|---------|-----------------------------------------|
| Gauge and Meter needles, Bar Panel fills and band stripes, LED Panel lamps | 1.4× on dark themes, 1.2× on light themes |
| Blinking alarm boxes, and the [annunciator](Aural-Alerts.md) bell in its fast flash | 1.7× |
| Thin strokes: plot curves and [frequency marker](Widget-Reference.md#frequency-markers) lines | 2.0× on dark themes, no boost on light themes |

Gauge and Meter band arcs stay at normal brightness, so they do not overpower the needle.

Serial Studio caps each level at the headroom the display reports, so a display with no HDR headroom looks the same as with the setting off. There is no brightness knob; the display decides.

On the **Plotting** tab, **Time Range** sets how far back a plot reaches, **Point Count** sets how many samples it keeps, and **UI Refresh Rate (Hz)** sets how many times per second the dashboard redraws (lower it on a slow computer). # Pro vs Free

An Arduino or ESP32 printing values with `Serial.println` over USB works fully in the free version: connection, plots, dashboard, CSV export. Pro starts at the other protocols (MQTT, Modbus, CAN, OPC UA and more), a handful of widgets and authoring features, and commercial use of the official binary.

An Arduino or ESP32 on a USB cable shows up as a serial port and uses the free **Serial/UART** driver. Raw USB and HID are for devices that do not present a serial port. Pick the bus type in the **Setup Panel**.

## Editions

Serial Studio comes in two forms:
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#0

docs.body:
- **Official binary.** The installer from [serial-studio.com](https://serial-studio.com) and GitHub releases. It runs without a license, and the free features work with no time limit. Without a license it is for personal, educational, and open-source use; commercial use needs a Pro license. Pro features are built in and unlock with a license or the 14-day trial (see [Pricing](#pricing)).
- **GPL build.** Compiled from source under the GPLv3. It contains the free feature set only and has no restriction on commercial use.

The **Free** column in the tables below applies to both: the official binary without a license, and a GPL build.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#1

docs.body:
## Quick summary

**Free:** Serial/UART, TCP, UDP, WebSocket, HTTP and Bluetooth LE; the widgets the table marks free (plots, gauges, compass, data grid, LED panel, terminal and more; GPS Map with its base layer only); the Project Editor without DBC import, dataset transforms, Variables or custom workspaces; CSV export and playback; the API Server.

**Pro adds:**

- Industrial and network protocols: MQTT, Modbus, CAN, OPC UA, S7, EtherNet/IP, IEC 104, audio, Raw USB, HID, Process I/O, and multi-device projects.
- More widgets: 3D Plot, Waterfall, Image View, Canvas, output controls, extra GPS map layers.
- Scripted data processing: dataset transforms, Variables, custom workspaces, DBC import.
- Recording and export: MDF4, Historian, InfluxDB, MQTT Publisher, console log export, WAV recording.
- Tools and support: file transfers, AI Assistant, Notification Log, operator deployments, email support.

| | Read the source | GPL modules (open source) | Pro modules are visible but proprietary |
| **Support** | | | |
| | Community Support (GitHub) | ✅ | ✅ |
| | Email Support | ❌ | ✅ |
| | Priority Bug Fixes | ❌ | ✅ |
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#4

docs.body:
Freeze dashboard works in Project File mode only. Turning freeze off always works, so an ended trial or license cannot leave a project frozen.

Binary (Direct) decoding is free in both editions. Set the source's **Data Conversion** to **Binary (Direct)** in the Project Editor; the parser then receives `frame` as a byte array (0-255). See [Frame Parser Scripting](Frame-Parser.md).

## Pro-Only Feature Details

### MQTT Integration

MQTT (Pro) connects to any MQTT broker, including the ones behind AWS IoT Core and Azure IoT Hub, as a subscriber (a device you connect to) and as a publisher (an export sink).
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#5

docs.body:
See [MQTT Topics & Semantics](MQTT-Topics.md) | [MQTT Subscriber](Drivers-MQTT.md) | [MQTT Publisher](MQTT-Publisher.md) | [Protocol Setup Guide](Protocol-Setup-Guides.md#mqtt-setup-pro)

### Modbus Protocol (RTU & TCP)

Modbus RTU and Modbus TCP (Pro) read and write registers on PLCs and other industrial equipment. A free build can reach the same PLC only through a raw TCP socket with a custom parser.

See [Protocol Setup Guide](Protocol-Setup-Guides.md#modbus-rtu-setup-pro) | [Modbus Driver](Drivers-Modbus.md)

### CAN Bus Support

CAN Bus (Pro) connects a CAN adapter and decodes signals automatically from an imported DBC file.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#6

docs.body:
See [Protocol Setup Guide](Protocol-Setup-Guides.md#can-bus-setup-pro) | [CAN Bus Driver](Drivers-CAN-Bus.md)

### OPC UA Client

OPC UA (Pro, IEC 62541) is the tag-oriented interface modern PLCs, SCADA servers and gateways expose over Ethernet. Enter an `opc.tcp://host:port` address to discover the server's endpoints, browse the address space, tick the tags to monitor, and generate a project from the selection, units and ranges included. Tags are subscribed, with automatic fallback to timed reads.

The bundled stack includes encryption in Sign and Sign & Encrypt modes.

See [OPC UA Driver](Drivers-OPC-UA.md)
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#7

docs.body:
### Siemens S7comm, EtherNet/IP, and IEC 60870-5-104

These three industrial drivers (Pro) appear in the **Setup Panel** bus type list next to Modbus and OPC UA.

See [S7 Driver](Drivers-S7.md) | [EtherNet/IP Driver](Drivers-EtherNet-IP.md) | [IEC 104 Driver](Drivers-IEC-104.md)

### Audio Input

Audio Input (Pro) captures a microphone or line-in live and shows its FFT spectrum. The usable bandwidth is half the sample rate you choose.

See [Audio Driver](Drivers-Audio.md) | [Protocol Setup Guide](Protocol-Setup-Guides.md#audio-input-setup-pro)

### 3D Plot Widget

The 3D Plot (Pro) draws X, Y, Z coordinates as a real-time scatter or line plot. It renders on the CPU, so it needs no GPU or OpenGL and runs on low-end hardware, including Raspberry Pi.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#8

docs.body:
See [Widget Reference - 3D Plot](Widget-Reference.md#3d-plot-pro)

### Waterfall Widget

The Waterfall (Pro) is a scrolling time-frequency plot (spectrogram) per dataset. Each row is one FFT magnitude spectrum, with the newest at the top. It reuses the dataset's FFT settings and offers fifteen color maps; the Y axis can follow another dataset for order tracking, such as RPM against frequency.

See [Widget Reference - Waterfall](Widget-Reference.md#waterfall-pro)

### Canvas Widget

The Canvas widget (Pro) is a user-scripted dashboard widget. The script defines a JavaScript `paint(ctx, w, h)` callback that renders into the widget's bitmap on every dashboard tick. Use it when no built-in widget covers the visualization.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#9

docs.body:
Each Canvas widget is bound to one project group and reads its datasets through a `datasets` global. The drawing API is Canvas2D-shaped, built-in templates (oscilloscope, dial gauge, artificial horizon and more) serve as starting points, and a 250 ms watchdog terminates a script whose call does not return.

See [Canvas Widget](Canvas-Widget.md)

### Raw USB

Raw USB (Pro) gives direct bulk, control, and isochronous access via libusb, bypassing the OS serial and HID layers. It fits custom firmware with bulk endpoints (STM32, TinyUSB) and devices that need vendor-specific control transfers.

See [Devices - Raw USB](Devices.md#raw-usb)
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#10

docs.body:
### HID Devices

HID (Pro) reads gamepads, joysticks, and custom USB HID firmware through hidapi, with no driver to write.

See [Devices - HID Devices](Devices.md#hid-device)

### Process I/O

Process I/O (Pro) spawns a child process and reads its stdout, or connects to a named pipe/FIFO from an external process. A Python script or a synthetic data generator can feed a dashboard with no hardware attached.

See [Devices - Process I/O](Devices.md#process-io)

### Image View Widget

Image View (Pro) shows a live JPEG/PNG/BMP/WebP feed on the dashboard beside other widgets.

- **Autodetect mode** finds JPEG/PNG frames by magic bytes with no configuration.
- **Manual delimiter mode** takes user-defined byte sequences for custom framing.
- Toolbar controls cover frame export, zoom, and filters.
- JPEG frames and CSV telemetry can share one connection.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#11

docs.body:
See [Widget Reference - Image View](Widget-Reference.md#image-view-pro) | [Camera Telemetry Example](https://github.com/Serial-Studio/Serial-Studio/tree/master/examples/Camera%20Telemetry)

### MDF4 File Support

MDF4 (MF4, Pro) is the standard binary format for measurement data in automotive testing, read by Vector CANape, NI DIAdem, and the MATLAB Vehicle Network Toolbox. Serial Studio exports sessions to MDF4, replays MDF4 files, and streams files larger than 1 GB.

See [MDF4 Playback and Export](MDF4.md)

### Output (Control) Widgets

Output widgets (Pro) send data *to* the device: buttons, toggles, sliders, knobs, text fields, and a freeform Output Panel. Each control runs a JavaScript transmit template (GCode, SCPI, Modbus, NMEA, CAN, SLCAN, GRBL, or custom binary) that converts the control's state into outgoing bytes. A Transmit Test Dialog previews the wire output before the real command is sent. In multi-device projects, each control targets a specific source.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#12

docs.body:
See [Output Controls](Output-Controls.md)

### Multi-Device Projects

Multi-device projects (Pro) hold several devices in one project file, each with its own bus type, connection settings, frame detection, and parser. All configured devices connect at the same time, each source's data routes to its own groups and widgets, and CSV/MDF4 export captures every source in one file. Sources are configured in the Project Editor under the Sources section.

See [Devices - Multi-device mode](Devices.md#multi-device-mode)

### Dataset Transforms, Variables, and Custom Workspaces

Three authoring features of the Project Editor (Pro). A [dataset transform](Dataset-Transforms.md) is a per-dataset JavaScript or Lua function that converts the raw parsed value before it reaches the dashboard. [Variables](Variables.md) are named values, grouped in tables, that transforms read and write. Custom workspaces replace the automatic dashboard tabs with ones the project defines.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#13

docs.body:
A project that contains a dataset transform or a Variables table needs a license or an active trial to connect, whatever created it. Right-click a dataset and choose **Remove Transform**, or delete the table, and the project connects free. The prompt shown at Connect lists how many transforms and tables the project has.

Opening the transform editor, creating, duplicating, or importing a table, adding a variable, and switching a project to custom workspaces also each need a license or an active trial. Bringing transforms back while connected without a license, by opening such a project, undoing the removal or switching to project mode, ends the session with the same prompt. A session already running when a license or trial ended keeps running until you disconnect. CSV playback is not affected, because playback never runs a transform.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#14

docs.body:
### Notification Log

The Notification Log (Pro) is the dashboard tool window that lists [notifications](Notifications.md) posted by scripts, alarm bands, and the API. Showing it needs a license or an active trial, as does posting to it.

### Historian

The Historian (Pro) records complete sessions (parsed frames, raw bytes, table snapshots, and project metadata) into a single SQLite `.db` file. It browses, tags, and exports stored sessions. The SQLite Player replays a recorded session through the live pipeline, so dashboards behave identically on recorded data. Session Reports turn the same database into a PDF with charts.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#15

docs.body:
See [Historian](Historian.md) | [Session Reports](Session-Reports.md)

### InfluxDB export

InfluxDB export (Pro) writes every parsed sample into an InfluxDB 2.x bucket over the database's HTTP write API while the capture runs. The InfluxDB Sink node in the Project Editor holds the server URL, organization, bucket and measurement; the API token goes to the machine's credential vault rather than the project file. Samples are sent as line protocol with the block's own nanosecond timestamps from a worker thread, so a slow server never blocks acquisition.

See [InfluxDB Export](InfluxDB.md)

### File Transmission
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#16

docs.body:
File Transmission (Pro) sends files to a connected device over the active connection, as plain text, raw binary, or via XMODEM, XMODEM-1K, YMODEM, or ZMODEM. ZMODEM includes crash recovery (ZRPOS).

See [File Transmission](File-Transmission.md)

### In-App AI Assistant

The AI Assistant (Pro) is a bring-your-own-key chat panel that reads the live dashboard and edits the project on request. Providers include Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Groq, OpenRouter, and Mistral, plus any OpenAI-compatible local server (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM) for offline use. Read-only commands run automatically; mutations show an Approve/Deny card; device control stays blocked unless the **Allow device control** toggle is on.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#17

docs.body:
See [AI Assistant](AI-Assistant.md)

### Operator Deployment Generation

Operator Deployment Generation (Pro) writes a single-icon entry point that opens Serial Studio with a specific project and a fixed set of command-line flags. The **Deploy** toolbar button writes either a `.ssdeploy` package (the default; one file carrying the project and the files it uses) or a shortcut to the `.ssproj` (`.lnk` on Windows, `.app` on macOS, `.desktop` on Linux). Both need a Pro build on the target machine, because the runtime flags a deployment writes are compiled out of GPL builds.

See [Operator Deployments](Operator-Deployments.md)

## Upgrading from Free to Pro

### Activation steps

1. Purchase a license from [serial-studio.com](https://serial-studio.com).
2. Download the official binary (if you were using a GPL build).
3. Open Serial Studio.
4. Open the Licensing dialog: click **About** in the toolbar, then **Manage License**. (Once the 14-day trial has expired, the prompt shown when a Pro feature is used has an **Activate License** button that opens the same dialog.)
5. Paste the license key from your purchase email and click **Activate**.

Pro features unlock once the key is accepted.

### Project files

Project files are unchanged between editions. Free projects open in Pro and vice versa, with no migration step.
docs.title: Pro-vs-Free#22

docs.body:
### Offline use

A network connection is needed for the initial activation. After that the license is tied to the hardware ID and is cached locally; Serial Studio revalidates it online when a connection is available, and a 30-day offline grace period covers machines that stay disconnected between checks.

A machine that can never reach the internet can be activated with a signed license file instead of connecting online. This is offered for lifetime and Test Stand licenses. See [Offline Activation](Offline-Activation.md).

## Academic use

There is no academic discount, because the free version covers coursework. Students, educators, and researchers can use the official binary without a license for educational and non-commercial research use, or build the GPL version from source. A university or research institution buys Pro when it needs the Pro features, commercial use of the official binary, or email support.

Yes. A build compiled from source with GPL modules only is GPLv3 software, and the GPLv3 permits commercial use. It excludes the Pro features. Those exist only in the official binary, which offers the 14-day trial; a GPL build cannot start it.

docs.body:
# Problem Center

You press **Connect**, bytes scroll through the console, and the dashboard stays empty. The Problem Center names the reason. It is a standing list of what is wrong with the current session: project mistakes that leave a widget empty, link conditions that corrupt or drop frames, script errors that stop parsing, and extension packages that failed to load. The Problem Center is available in every edition; a few audio and MQTT broker diagnostics exist only in Pro.

## Overview

Each finding comes from a check (each has an id like `link.statistics`) and states the condition, the concrete cause, and what to change. Most carry a **Go To** button that opens the Project Editor at the dataset, group, action, or source involved. On every run a checker's findings are replaced wholesale, so a condition that has been fixed disappears from the list by itself.
docs.title: Problem-Center#0

docs.body:
Press **Ctrl+K** (**Cmd+K** on macOS) to open the [command palette](Command-Palette.md), type `Problem Center`, and press Enter. Both entries work from the main window, the dashboard, and the Project Editor:

| Palette entry | Effect |
|---------------|--------|
| **Problem Center** | Opens the window with the findings that stand right now. |
| **Connection Diagnostics** | Runs every connection check this build supports, then opens the same window with the results. |

When a run finds new problems, a **Problems detected** notification says how many. While Serial Studio is skipping some incoming data, the dashboard taskbar shows a red dot, and the `parse-thinning` finding explains it.
docs.title: Problem-Center#1

docs.body:
### An example

A frame is one message from your device, such as `1,2,3` followed by a newline. An Arduino prints `Serial.println("1,2,3")`, but the project waits for a `;` end delimiter. Bytes arrive, no frame ever completes, and after three seconds the list shows:

- **Severity**: Error, from the checker `link.statistics`.
- **Title**: Data is arriving but no frames are extracted.
- **Cause**: the link has received a number of bytes over the last few seconds without completing a single frame.
- **Remedy**: check the frame detection mode and the start/end delimiters of the source; they must match what the device sends.
docs.title: Problem-Center#2

docs.body:
**Go To** opens the source in the Project Editor. Fix the delimiter and the row is gone on the next check. You do not need to dismiss the row; the next check removes it.

## The window

The header counts the standing findings as errors, warnings, and notices, and a filter narrows the list to one severity. A notice is shown as **Information** on its row. Three buttons act on the list:

| Button | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| **Run Diagnostics** | Starts a Connection Diagnostics run over every supported bus. Reads **Running Diagnostics...** and stays disabled until the probes settle. |
| **Refresh** | Re-runs every checker at once, regardless of what normally triggers it, including the on-demand connection checks. |
| **Clear** | Drops every standing finding without re-running anything. Conditions that still hold return on their next trigger. |
docs.title: Problem-Center#3

docs.body:
Each row shows the severity icon, the title, the checker that produced it, the explanation, and the remedy. **Go To** appears on findings that point at a project entity. The footer reads `Last checked at <time>` after the first run.

## Reading the list when the dashboard is blank
docs.title: Problem-Center#4

docs.body:
1. Open the Problem Center. An error-severity finding from `link.statistics` or `script.parser` names the stage where data stops. A dashboard that stays empty while the console scrolls is almost always a delimiter mismatch.
   - `link.statistics` with **Data is arriving but no frames are extracted**: the delimiters do not match what the device sends.
   - A frames-without-values finding: the frame parser returns nothing.
   - `script.parser`: the parser was switched off after running too long.
2. With no link findings, look for `project.*` errors: a dangling axis or a dataset with no frame position renders an empty widget with no message anywhere else.
3. With no findings at all and no data in the console, click **Run Diagnostics**, or run **Connection Diagnostics** from the command palette. A port permission failure or an unresolved host name shows up here, with the command or setting that fixes it.
4. Fix the cause, then click **Refresh**. A cleared condition leaves the list.
docs.title: Problem-Center#5

docs.body:
## Checkers and their triggers

The rest of this page is reference: look a code up when you see it in the list. A frame is one message from your device, such as `12.5,40.1` followed by a newline. The parser turns it into a list of numbers, and each dataset reads one position of that list, its frame index (the dataset's position in the parsed list).

| Trigger | Checkers |
|---------|----------|
| Project loaded, edited, or saved | `project.*`, `extension.catalog`, `alarms.sounds` |
| Once a second while connected | `link.statistics`, `script.*`, `alarms.sounds`, `project.licensing` |
| **Refresh**, or the API command `problems.run` | Every checker, including `diagnostics.*` |
| **Run Diagnostics**, or a failed connection attempt | `diagnostics.*` only |
docs.title: Problem-Center#6

docs.body:
One checker lists at most 50 findings per run; past that, its last row is a notice counting the hidden ones.

### Project checkers
docs.title: Problem-Center#7

docs.body:
| Checker | Reports |
|---------|---------|
| `project.frame-index` | Error: a dataset whose frame index is zero or negative, so it can never read a value. Warning: two datasets of the same source that read the same frame index with the same group widget and the same dataset widget, so one repeats the other exactly. Reading one value twice to show it two ways, for example in a Data Grid and a Multi-Plot, is supported and not reported. |
| `project.empty-group` | Warning: a group with no datasets and no output widgets. |
| `project.group-widget` | Warning: a group whose widget cannot use its datasets. An Accelerometer or Gyroscope needs exactly three datasets tagged X, Y and Z, a 3D Plot needs X, Y and Z, a GPS Map needs lat and lon, and a Data Grid, Multi-Plot or Bar Panel needs at least one enabled dataset. Widgets bind datasets by tag, not by order. |
| `project.reference` | A plot X-axis, waterfall axis, workspace tile, action, or output widget that points at a dataset or source that no longer exists. Error for axes, actions and outputs; warning for a tile. |
| `project.numeric-range` | Warning: a plot, widget, or FFT range whose minimum is above its maximum, an LED threshold outside the dataset's range, or an inverted alarm band. |
| `project.alias` | Warning: two datasets sharing one alias, so scripts and the API can reach only one of them by name. |
| `project.licensing` | Warning: a device that needs Serial Studio Pro in a session without a license or trial, so it cannot connect. Also runs on the one-second tick, so it reacts when the license state changes without a project edit. |
| `extension.catalog` | Warning: an extension catalog entry that lists files without sha256 digests, so an install could not tell a genuine download from a replaced one. |
docs.title: Problem-Center#8

docs.body:
### Link checkers

`link.statistics` samples the frame reader counters once a second. A condition marked "sustained" must hold for 3 consecutive samples before it is reported. Checksum and drop totals count from the moment the link opened, so a bad burst early on keeps its warning.
docs.title: Problem-Center#9

docs.body:
| Finding | Severity | Condition |
|---------|----------|-----------|
| `bytes-without-frames` | Error | Bytes arrive but no frame is detected (sustained). The delimiters or the frame detection mode do not match the stream. |
| `frames-without-values` | Error | Frames are detected but the parser produces no values (sustained). Not raised when every dataset is computed, because that parser feeds Variables Tables and returns no values by design. |
| `short-frames` | Warning | Frames carry fewer values than the highest frame index the project maps for that source (sustained). The datasets above the received count keep their last value and look frozen. One finding per affected source; **Go To** opens the first starved dataset. |
| `checksum-failures` | Warning | At least 20 checksummed frames have been seen and 5% or more failed. |
| `dropped-frames` | Warning | The frame queue overflowed and frames were discarded. Lower the data rate, simplify the frame parser, or put fewer widgets on the dashboard. |
| `parse-thinning` | Warning | Data arrives faster than the scripts can process it, so Serial Studio is skipping some incoming data to keep up. Simplify the frame parser or lower the data rate. |
| `buffer-overflow` | Warning | Bytes were discarded because the receive buffer filled before they were read. Lower the data rate, or confirm the frames end with the configured delimiter. |
docs.title: Problem-Center#10

docs.body:
### Script and extension checkers

| Checker | Reports |
|---------|---------|
| `script.parser` | The frame parser was switched off by the watchdog after exceeding its time budget on too many consecutive frames, so its source produces nothing until the script is fixed and reloaded (error), or the parser keeps failing (warning). |
| `script.transform` | A dataset value transform is producing errors (warning). |
| `script.control` | The project's [Control Loop](Control-Loop.md) stopped on a runtime error and drives nothing until you fix it and reconnect (warning). Any alarm it held open needs an acknowledge. |
| `extension.widget` | A widget extension package that could not be loaded. The [Widget Extension Development](Widget-Extension-Development.md) page lists each cause. |
| `alarms.sounds` | An alarm sound file that cannot be used, aural alerts switched off while the project defines alarms, or no usable audio output device (warnings). See [Aural Alerts](Aural-Alerts.md). |
docs.title: Problem-Center#11

docs.body:
## Connection Diagnostics

Connection Diagnostics is part of the Problem Center. Open it with the **Connection Diagnostics** palette entry or the **Run Diagnostics** button. It asks "can this machine connect at all" rather than "is the project right". The checks only look: they never open a data link or change a setting. When the fix is a shell command, the finding prints it so you can copy it.

Checks come in two classes:

| Class | Covers | Timing |
|-------|--------|--------|
| Instant | Serial port presence and device-node permissions, Bluetooth adapter power and permission, audio backend and input devices, host and port configuration | Complete before the window opens |
| Probing | Host name resolution and a bounded TCP connect to the configured network or MQTT endpoint | Run in the background, 2 s for the lookup and 3 s for the connect per endpoint, 15 s for the whole run |
docs.title: Problem-Center#12

docs.body:
Runs also start automatically when a connection attempt fails: the instant checks run at once, and the probes run at most once per 30 s per bus so a retry loop cannot flood a broker. Connecting successfully clears that bus's findings.

Results appear in the Problem Center under the checkers `diagnostics.serial`, `diagnostics.bluetooth`, `diagnostics.network`, `diagnostics.broker` (Pro), and `diagnostics.audio` (Pro). The MQTT broker probe and the audio checks are Pro; the other findings are in every edition. A failed check shows as **Error** in the window.
docs.title: Problem-Center#13

docs.body:
| Finding | Severity | Meaning |
|---------|----------|---------|
| `port-access-denied` | Error | This account cannot read and write the serial port. On Linux the remedy names the owning group and the `usermod` command to run, or the udev rule to add when group membership is not the cause. |
| `no-serial-ports` | Warning | The system reports no serial ports. The remedy names the USB-serial driver to install for the adapter's chip, per platform. |
| `selected-port-missing` | Warning | The port selected in the device setup is no longer reported by the system. |
| `ble-permission-denied` | Error | The system refused Serial Studio permission to use Bluetooth. |
| `ble-adapter-off` | Error | No powered-on Bluetooth adapter was found. |
| `ble-unsupported` | Warning | The operating system build provides no Bluetooth Low Energy support. |
| `host-not-configured` | Warning | The network or MQTT source has no host name or address. |
| `port-not-configured` | Warning | The host has no port number. |
| `host-not-resolved` | Error | The host name did not resolve to an address. |
| `connection-refused` | Error | The host answered and refused the port, so the service is not listening there. |
| `endpoint-timed-out` | Error | The host did not answer within the time allowed for the check. |
| `audio-permission-denied` (Pro) | Error | The system refused Serial Studio permission to record audio. |
| `audio-input-missing` (Pro) | Warning | The selected audio input device is no longer reported by the backend. |
| `audio-backend-failed` (Pro) | Error | The system audio backend did not initialize. |
| `no-audio-inputs` (Pro) | Warning | The audio backend reports no capture device. |

The same list is readable over the API Server (off by default, port 7777; enable it first): `problems.list` returns the findings with their codes, `problems.run` re-runs the checkers, `problems.listCheckers` names each checker and its triggers, and `diagnostics.run` / `diagnostics.status` drive a connection check and poll it.
